input.title: ZM audience read memo - cards earlier
input.bodyText:
ZM audience read: cards earlier
Julia Lawson, Oct 1 2025

THE CALL: CASUAL LEAD. HOLD THE CARDS EARLIER CHANGE.

Per Leonard's rule (casual lead = hold, RPG lead = keep, no clear lead = keep), the friend sessions show a clear casual lead, so the cards earlier change from Monday is on hold. The tutorial and level order work for it does not go ahead. This covers the current game only. Iterate or pivot is a separate, later call.

1. The numbers behind the call
Lead = higher mean star rating over counted sessions. Each audience needs at least 6 counted sessions, and a gap under 0.25 means no clear lead (ZM audience read criteria). The observer's audience label is used as recorded.

- Casual: 9 counted sessions, 34.5 stars in total, mean 3.83 (ZOM-595, 600, 602, 605, 621, 622, 625, 626, 627)
- RPG: 8 counted sessions, 27.0 stars in total, mean 3.38 (ZOM-589, 592, 597, 598, 599, 604, 623, 624)
- Gap: 0.46 in casual's favour. Both audiences clear the 6-session minimum and the gap is well over 0.25, so this is a clear casual lead.

2. What counted and what didn't (60 sessions logged, 17 counted, 43 not counted)
Rules applied: Leonard's feedback note (25-45 year olds, no coaching), his follow-ups in #zombie-design (game-industry people don't count; friends includes family, neighbours and classmates), and the ZM session stability gate (dev builds don't count; Samsung sessions only count once a clean pass has run on the device). All of these apply to sessions already run.

- 9 not counted, game industry (ZOM-568 to 576, Brian's Sep 22 group). Brian confirmed his "Kadikoy ekibi" all work at mobile game companies. These were all RPG, mean 4.83.
- 13 not counted, coached (ZOM-607 to 619, Claire's Sep 26 group). Claire told me she walked everyone through the cards, items and grenade timing before they played. Her form said "no coaching", but her later mail corrects that. These were all RPG, mean 4.65.
- 10 not counted, dev build (ZOM-577 to 586, Robert's Sep 23 group). Android 0.3.127 (1943) never went through a store. Store builds are Android 0.3.127 (127) and iOS 0.3.38 / 0.3.40. These were all casual, mean 2.45.
- 11 not counted, Samsung with no device pass (ZOM-587, 588, 590, 591, 593, 594, 596, 601, 603, 606, 620). The only pass so far is Arthur's Vision Bot job (PR #476). On the PR, Arthur says it runs in Unity editor play mode with no phone involved, so it covers no handset. These were all casual, mean 2.36.
- 17 counted: aged 25-45, not in games, store build, non-Samsung phone, no coaching reported.
Ticket close-out follows my log note: counted goes to Done, not counted goes to Canceled. Following Robert, the 21 sessions dropped for a technical reason (build or device) have a re-run note. The 22 dropped for other reasons are closed with no re-run.

Robustness: the sessions that drop out pull in opposite directions (the excluded RPG sessions are high, the excluded casual ones are low). The read stands on the 17 that pass every rule.

3. Context only (sessions decide)
Playtestcloud panel (puzzlesvszombies-3 iOS and -4 Android, as Leonard forwarded them). These players were recruited as US/CA/UK adults playing mobile RPG or 3D match games. Counted as stars per player, one number each. Player 8's rating (1) is void because they rated an app freeze, not the game, so it comes out of both the sum and the count. 9 valid ratings, 30.0 stars, mean 3.33. That is in line with the 3-3.5 Leonard's note started from.

ZM retention: install-weighted D7 of 9.09%. That covers mature cohorts only (those with a D14 figure), both platforms pooled: 47 weekly cohorts, 6,040 installs, install weeks Apr 7 to Sep 15 2025 (ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION). The simple cohort mean of 8.69% is not the figure to quote.

Neither the panel nor retention changes the call. Per the criteria, sessions decide.

4. What happens next
- Cards earlier: on hold. Card intro stays where it is.
- Brian: tutorial and level order work for cards earlier stops.
- Observers with a re-run note (Robert; Oliver, Owen, Samuel and Calvin for the Samsung sessions) can re-run on a store build and a non-Samsung phone, or on Samsung once a real device pass exists.

Sources: ZM audience sessions workbook (Log and Register tabs), ZM audience read criteria, ZM session stability gate, ZM sessions log note, observers' notes docs and form mails, ZOM-568 to 627, #zombie-design threads, PR #476, Snowflake USER_COHORT_RETENTION.
